name: Pennsylvania
note: The funeral director or other person in charge of interment files the death certificate with a local registrar within four business days, after the attending physician, CRNP or PA (or the coroner, for sudden, violent, suspicious or unattended deaths) supplies the medical certification. No body may be disposed of without the registrar's permit. The Department of Health sends a monthly electronic file of adult resident deaths to the Department of State, where county boards of election use it to remove voters. Other agencies get data only on request, and certified copies are limited to applicants with a direct interest.

steps.title: Professional nurse pronounces death and releases the body
steps.who: A registered professional nurse involved in the patient's direct care, for a natural death of a patient under a physician's or CRNP's care when the physician or CRNP cannot be present within a reasonable time.
steps.summary: The nurse may pronounce death under the Uniform Determination of Death Act and release the body to a funeral director after notifying the attending physician or CRNP and a family member, but may not determine the cause of death. Unanticipated deaths go to the coroner.

steps.title: Hospice practical nurse pronounces death
steps.who: A trained licensed practical nurse employed by a licensed hospice, for a hospice patient with a valid Do Not Resuscitate order.
steps.summary: Added in 2024; the practical nurse may pronounce and release the body after notice to the attending physician or CRNP and a family member.

steps.title: Refer the death to the coroner
steps.who: The local registrar, the person in charge of interment, or any other person having knowledge of the death.
steps.trigger: No qualified practitioner attended the last illness or the practitioner cannot supply the data; the death was sudden, violent, suspicious or not from natural causes; or the certifier would be a member of the decedent's immediate family.
steps.summary: In every referral the coroner investigates immediately and supplies the medical certification.

steps.title: Attending practitioner supplies the medical certification
steps.who: The physician, certified registered nurse practitioner or physician assistant who attended the deceased during the last illness (or a hospital staff dentist in limited cases); not a member of the decedent's immediate family.
steps.trigger: The person in charge of interment seeks the certification.
steps.summary: The attending practitioner certifies the cause by signature; if the usual certifier is immediate family, the case goes to another practitioner or the coroner.

steps.title: Coroner supplies the medical certification
steps.summary: The coroner supplies the data and medical certification after an immediate investigation. An unidentified body cannot receive a death certificate until a DNA sample is submitted to the Pennsylvania State Police.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate with a local registrar
steps.who: The funeral director or other person in charge of interment or of removal of the body from the registration district, with personal particulars from the person best acquainted with the facts.
steps.trigger: The death or finding of the body.

deadline.text: within four (4) business days after the death (s. 504: 96 hours)

steps.summary: The certificate is filed with any local registrar or the State Registrar, always before a disposal permit issues. Neglecting a duty under the Act is a summary offence (fine $50-$300); false information is a misdemeanour.

steps.title: Registrar issues the permit for disposal
steps.who: A local registrar or the State Registrar; registrars may issue blank presigned permits to funeral directors only.
steps.summary: No body may be disposed of without a permit. The cemetery or crematory may not inter or cremate without it and must return the endorsed permit to the registrar within ten days.

steps.title: Local registrar transmits original death certificates to the Department of Health
steps.summary: Local registrars send the originals to the Department of Health under its rules and may issue certified copies of death certificates in their possession for 90 days after the original is issued.

steps.title: Department of Health sends a monthly electronic file of adult resident deaths to the Department of State
steps.who: The Department of Health, to the Department of State.
steps.trigger: Deaths of residents aged 18 or over in the preceding month.
steps.summary: The file carries name, gender, last address, date of birth, county of residence, date and county of death, state file number and the last four SSN digits.

steps.title: County boards of election remove deceased voters through the SURE system
steps.who: The Department of State loads the file into the Statewide Uniform Registry of Electors (SURE); county boards of election act on it.
steps.summary: The death data entered in SURE is used by county boards to remove deceased individuals from the rolls.

steps.title: Department of Health discloses death data to other government agencies on request
steps.who: The Department of Health, to federal, state or municipal agencies.
steps.trigger: An agency request in the conduct of official duty.
steps.summary: This is the general route for state benefit, tax and licensing agencies to obtain death data; no specific feed is named in the Act.

steps.title: Use of death records for supervised research
steps.summary: Records may be used for research under strict supervision. There is no general verification service for banks or insurers in state law.

steps.title: Certified copies only for applicants with a direct interest
steps.who: The Department of Health; local registrars authorised to issue copies of death certificates.
steps.summary: Vital records are not open to public inspection. A certified copy issues only to an applicant with a direct interest whose information is needed to determine personal or property rights. Death records become public 50 years after death and pass to the State Archives.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Four business days after death or the finding of the body (s. 501); s. 504 separately says 96 hours. Filing must precede the disposal permit.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director or other person in charge of interment or removal files; the person best acquainted with the facts supplies personal information.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate; coroner referral only for the section 503 cases.

electronicRegistration.note: The Vital Statistics Law does not mention electronic registration; the Department of Health's EDRS rules (28 Pa. Code ch. 1) could not be read because pacodeandbulletin.gov is blocked.

governmentPropagation.note: State law requires only the monthly death file to the Department of State for voter removal; other agencies may request data. SSA feeds are in the federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Direct interest needed to determine personal or property rights; public after 50 years.

gaps: 28 Pa. Code ch. 1 (Department of Health vital statistics regulations, including electronic filing and who has a 'direct interest') could not be read: www.pacodeandbulletin.gov and pacodeandbulletin.gov are refused by the egress proxy (CONNECT 403), as is www.pacode.com.
Sections 501 (four business days) and 504 (96 hours) give different filing deadlines for the same certificate; both are recorded.

No Pennsylvania statute found requiring PennDOT to cancel a driver's licence, the Department of Revenue, or the Department of Human Services (Medicaid) to be notified of deaths; not searched beyond the Vital Statistics Law.
The state feed to SSA is not in the Vital Statistics Law; left to the us-federal layer.
Coroner duties outside the Vital Statistics Law (County Code, 16 P.S. § 1237) were not read.
privateSectorVerification is deliberately omitted so the us-federal value (LADMF) applies; Pennsylvania law adds only supervised research access (s. 805).
35 P.S. § 450.xxx numbers are the Purdon's equivalents of the Act's section numbers; the official palegis.us text shows only the Act's own section numbers.
